title: The Tectonic Collision That Accidentally Cooled Our Entire Planet
description: Discover how the tectonic rise of the Himalayas acted as a colossal carbon sink, stripping greenhouse gases from the atmosphere and plunging Earth into a global cooling phase.
instagram_caption:
Did you know mountains could cool an entire planet? 🏔️ When the Himalayas rose 50 million years ago, they didn't just touch the sky—they acted as a giant planetary vacuum, pulling carbon dioxide out of the atmosphere and shaping the modern climate we live in today. Nature’s ultimate thermostat! 

#Himalayas #EarthScience #ClimateHistory #Geology #NatureWonders #ScienceFacts

segments.narration: The Himalayas did the unthinkable, acting as a colossal planetary vacuum that sucked greenhouse gases right out of the sky.
Fifty million years ago, a massive tectonic collision slammed India into Asia, forcing these giant mountains upward.
This sudden uplift exposed raw minerals, triggering chemical reactions with rainwater that washed carbon away, burying it deep in the ocean.
broll_queries: river water carrying sediment close up

segments.narration: This relentless geological drain stripped the atmosphere of its heat-trapping gases, thinning Earth's protective warm blanket.
With the greenhouse insulation gone, global temperatures plunged, wrapping the poles in ice.
Today, these peaks still regulate our climate, acting as a giant thermostat that prevents runaway warming.
